# hermes-nabu

> Unofficial thin-client firmware that turns the Home Assistant Voice Preview
> Edition (ESP32-S3) into a push-to-talk satellite for Hermes Agent. This file
> tells an AI coding agent (Claude Code or similar) how to set up the Hermes
> host, build and flash the firmware, and configure the device over USB.

Work through the steps in order. Each step names the check that proves it
worked; do not move on until that check passes. Steps marked HUMAN need the
user's hands or secrets: stop, explain what to do, and wait.

## Ground rules

- Ask before flashing. Flashing overwrites the stock firmware; the user can
  restore it later with the official web installer (see Recovery).
- Never write Wi-Fi passwords, Hermes tokens or API keys into files, commits,
  `sdkconfig.defaults` or menuconfig. Settings live in the device's NVS only.
- Only one process can own the serial port. Before flashing or sending console
  commands, check that no `idf.py monitor` holds it
  (`fuser -v /dev/ttyACM0`). If one does, ask the user to quit it with
  `Ctrl+]`; do not kill it.
- `idf.py monitor` is interactive and needs a TTY. Use it only by asking the
  user to run it; drive the console yourself with the helper in step 5.
- Run every build or flash command inside the dev shell: `nix develop
  --command <cmd>` (or rely on direnv if it is already active).

## 1. Check prerequisites

- Nix with flakes. `nix develop --command idf.py --version` prints ESP-IDF
  v5.5.2.
- Hermes Agent installed on a host (this machine or another) with
  `hermes --version` working there.
- Voice PE connected over USB-C with a data cable. Linux shows it as
  `/dev/ttyACM*`; `ls /dev/serial/by-id/` lists an
  `Espressif_USB_JTAG_serial_debug_unit` entry.
- The device and the Hermes host share a network the device can reach on
  2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.

## 2. Set up Hermes on the host

Run on the computer where Hermes runs. If that is not this machine, give the
user the commands instead of running them.

1. Install the Gadget plugin pinned to the same SDK commit as the firmware.
   Read the commit from `main/idf_component.yml`
   (`hermes_gadget_core.version`), then:

   ```sh
   hermes plugins install https://github.com/Adolanium/hermes-gadget-sdk.git#plugin --ref <commit> --enable
   hermes gateway setup        # choose "Hermes Gadget", accept the restart
   ```

2. Get the device URL:

   ```sh
   hermes gadget info
   ```

   Check: it prints a URL like `ws://<host>:8765/gadget`. If it shows
   `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`, use the host's LAN IP or hostname instead; the
   device cannot reach the host's loopback.

3. Make sure the gateway keeps running (`hermes gateway restart` for the
   service, or `hermes gateway run` in a terminal) and that the host firewall
   allows the gadget port (8765 by default).

4. Speech: the device sends raw audio, Hermes does STT and TTS. Check that
   `stt:` and `tts:` are configured in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (or run
   `hermes tools` / `hermes setup`). Non-WAV TTS output needs `ffmpeg` on the
   host.

Optional settings live under `platforms.gadget.extra` in
`~/.hermes/config.yaml` (`port`, `path`, `speak_replies`, `tls_cert`,
`tls_key`). Port, path or TLS changes need a gateway restart. An optional
shared secret goes in `~/.hermes/.env` as `GADGET_ACCESS_TOKEN`; the device
then needs the same value in its `token` setting.

## 3. Build

```sh
nix develop --command idf.py build
```

Check: the build ends with `Project build complete` and writes
`build/hermes-nabu.bin`. The first build downloads the pinned components into
`managed_components/`; never edit files there.

## 4. Flash (ask first)

Confirm with the user, then:

```sh
nix develop --command idf.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 flash
```

Check: esptool ends with `Hard resetting via RTS pin...` and no error.

HUMAN, only if esptool cannot connect (`Failed to connect`, `No serial data
received`): ask the user to put the device in bootloader mode and retry:

1. Unplug USB-C.
2. Hold the center button.
3. Plug USB-C back in.
4. Release the button after a moment.

The port name can change after re-plugging; re-check `/dev/ttyACM*`. After a
flash from bootloader mode, ask the user to unplug and replug once so the new
firmware boots normally.

## 5. Configure the device over serial

The firmware opens its console (`gadget>` prompt) only when a USB host is
attached at boot. Every command answers with one line that starts with `@`:
`@ok`, `@error`, `@status {json}`, `@value {json}`, `@help`. Log lines
interleave, so read until the `@` line.

Send one command at a time with this helper. Opening the port with DTR and RTS
low keeps the ESP32-S3 from resetting.

```sh
nix develop --command python - /dev/ttyACM0 status <<'EOF'
import sys, time, serial
REPLY_TIMEOUT_S = 5
port, line = sys.argv[1], " ".join(sys.argv[2:])
link = serial.Serial()
link.port, link.baudrate, link.timeout = port, 115200, 0.5
link.dtr = link.rts = False
link.open()
link.reset_input_buffer()
link.write((line + "\r\n").encode())
deadline = time.time() + REPLY_TIMEOUT_S
while time.time() < deadline:
    text = link.readline().decode(errors="replace").strip()
    if "@" in text:
        print(text[text.index("@"):])
        break
else:
    sys.exit(f"no reply to '{line}' from {port}")
EOF
```

Replace `status` with the command to send. Configure in this order:

1. `set server <url from hermes gadget info>` → `@ok server`
2. `set wifi_ssid <ssid>` → `@ok wifi_ssid`
3. HUMAN: the Wi-Fi password. Ask the user to set it themselves so it never
   passes through your context: they run
   `nix develop --command idf.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 monitor`, type
   `set wifi_pass <password>` at the `gadget>` prompt, and quit with `Ctrl+]`.
   Then check with `get wifi_pass` → `@value {"key":"wifi_pass","value":"<set>"}`.
4. Optional: `set name <name>`, `set volume <0-100>`, `set token <value>` (only
   if `GADGET_ACCESS_TOKEN` is set on the host; same HUMAN rule as the
   password).
5. `status` → check `"network":true` and `"phase":"online"` (it passes
   through `no_network`, `connecting` and `handshake` first; an `error` field
   names a fatal problem such as a rejected token).

`help` lists all commands and keys. Settings keys: `name server token
talk_mode volume wifi_ssid wifi_pass` (`brightness`, `screen_timeout` and
`battery_display` exist in the core but do nothing on this board). Setting a
key to an empty value clears it.

## 6. Pair with Hermes

When the device reaches Hermes for the first time, `status` contains a
`pairing_code`, and the serial log shows
`state: pairing, code <CODE> (approve: hermes pairing approve gadget <CODE>)`.

On the Hermes host:

```sh
hermes gadget pair                         # asks before approving
# or: hermes pairing approve gadget <CODE>
```

Check: `status` shows `"paired":true`, and `hermes gadget devices` lists the
device without "waiting to pair".

## 7. End-to-end test (HUMAN)

Ask the user to hold the center button, speak, and release. Check: the LED
ring moves through listening → thinking → speaking and the reply plays on the
speaker. The hardware mute switch blocks capture and shows red marks on the
ring; it must be off for this test.

## Troubleshooting

- `"phase"` stays `connecting`: wrong `server` URL, gateway not running, firewall, or a
  loopback address. Re-check step 2, then send `reconnect`.
- `diag` prints connection details as JSON. Its `net` object shows the joined
  access point (`ssid`, `rssi`, `channel`), `mac`, `ip`, `mask`, `gw` and the
  `dns` servers DHCP handed out. Check these first when a hostname fails to
  resolve (`getaddrinfo() returns 202` in the log).
- `@error device busy`: the app task did not answer within 3 s; retry.
- No `gadget>` reply at all: the device booted without a USB host. Replug
  USB-C, or reset it with `nix develop --command esptool.py -p /dev/ttyACM0
  run`.
- Start over: `factory-reset` erases the device key and all settings, then
  replug. The device needs pairing again; remove the old entry with
  `hermes gadget forget <device>` on the host.

## Recovery

Bootloader mode (step 4) always works, so the device cannot be bricked by a
bad build. Restore the stock Home Assistant firmware with the official web
installer in Chrome or Edge: https://esphome.github.io/home-assistant-voice-pe/
